item.title: MAP: The local tax you will have to pay in Sweden in 2026
item.description: Residents of 16 Swedish municipalities will pay more local tax in 2026, while 45 municipalities will pay less tax. What's the situation where you live?

item.title: What we know about the suspected murder of a 25-year-old woman in Sweden
item.description: A 25-year-old woman was found dead over the weekend after a search in Salem, southwest of Stockholm. A 26-year-old suspect with previous convictions has been detained on suspicion of murder.

item.title: When are you eligible for a Swedish pension?
item.description: Sweden's pension system is set to change from 2026. What are the rules and how can you get your pension when the time comes?

item.title: 'Brexit is not done': How Britons in Europe are still fighting for their rights
item.description: Five years on from the end of free movement, Britons living throughout Europe are still dealing with the consequences of Brexit. Fiona Godfrey, from British in Europe, tells The Local the battle to secure rights is still ongoing and that things could get more complicated.

item.title: What's open and closed in Sweden over the New Year holiday?
item.description: Most workers in Sweden have New Year's Eve and New Year's Day off, but how are shops, Systembolaget and public transport affected?

item.title: Swedish word of the day: god fortsättning
item.description: Here's a word you can use to greet friends, neighbours and colleagues around this time of year.

item.title: CHECKLIST: Everything you need to do when you move house in Sweden
item.description: Whether you're moving to a new rented apartment or have bought your home, there are lots of things to keep track of to help the move go smoothly.

item.title: What can you do with your kids in Sweden before term starts again?
item.description: You might already be back at work after the Christmas break, but your kids aren’t necessarily back at school yet. What can you do with them during the rest of the holidays to keep them occupied?

item.title: Tax cuts, longer citizenship waits and an election: What changes in Sweden in 2026
item.description: Sweden's government is bringing in far-reaching tax cuts, lower daycare fees, an increase in the wait for citizenship to 8 years, and on top of all that, there's a general election. Here's what's happening in Sweden in 2026.

item.title: Why do the Swedes watch Ivanhoe on New Year's Day?
item.description: A lot of Sweden's holiday traditions centre around the TV, and one of the most baffling takes place on the afternoon of January 1st. What is it about the 1982 adaptation of Ivanhoe that gets people tuning in, year after year?
